question: This New Year’s Eve, unsafe fireworks of Chinese origin – banned in Germany and Austria – were once again freely sold in Czech border regions. Year after year, the lack of border controls means that such sales result in hundreds of severe lifelong injuries in the aforementioned neighbouring countries, with young people most commonly affected.

Please can the Commission explain why, in its capacity as guardian of consumer protection in the large EU internal market, it has still not taken steps to put a stop to these life-threatening practices?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.6.2024) Safety and security of fireworks in the EU are the main objectives of the Pyrotechnic Articles Directive1. Only pyrotechnic articles satisfying the requirements of the Directive, in particular essential safety requirements, can be made available on the market.

In addition, each type of fireworks, before placing on the market, must undergo the appropriate conformity assessment procedure. Member States have to ensure that the requirements are enforced so that all fireworks, those manufactured in the EU and those imported, are safe and sold only to customers belonging to the appropriate age group or having the required specialist knowledge.

Coordination between Member States is facilitated through the administrative cooperation group for market surveillance and the expert group for pyrotechnic articles. Furthermore, fireworks presenting a high hazard (category F4), such as flash bangers are prohibited for sale to the general public throughout the EU and are allowed to be made available to persons with specialist knowledge only.

Member States can also prohibit or restrict the possession, use and/or sale to the general public of certain types of fireworks (for example bangers, categories F2 or F3), that comply with the requirements of the Directive, if justified on grounds of public order, security, health and safety, or environmental protection.

The scope of imposed restrictions may vary in different Member States – Austria and Germany require permissions for fireworks category 3 and 4, which is not the case in the Czech Republic. The Commission is currently evaluating the Directive2, which will notably assess whether the rules are still fit for purpose.
1 Directive 2013/29/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 June 2013 on the harmonisation of

the laws of the Member States relating to the making available on the market of pyrotechnic articles: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2013/29/oj 2 See the closed Call for evidence: https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-yoursay/initiatives/13640-EU-rules-on-pyrotechnic-articles-evaluation_en and the launch of the public consultation: https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/13640-EU-rules-on-pyrotechnicarticles-evaluation/public-consultation_en
